headline: High: shared broad egress and overlapping secret-bearing workflows create default data-leak and cascading-error risk; LightAgent’s MCP/tool-calling can amplify Kotaemon outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, and chat transcripts, while LightAgent supports MCP and tool-calling with runtime hooks that can observe or replace payloads. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Kotaemon content is forwarded into LightAgent workflows. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Kotaemon outputs are copied into LightAgent prompts or MCP payloads
IF LightAgent parses document text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding between agents
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor
Require human review before LightAgent executes any imported text
Log provenance for every cross-agent payload
requires-engineering: add content-type and trust labels end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, and LightAgent handles conversations, memory, trace data, and tool results while using broad network egress. If they share a workspace or exchange outputs, sensitive content can flow from either agent into the other’s logs or remote APIs. Because both sides have broad egress and secret-bearing surfaces, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or copied artifacts
IF either agent sends imported content to a third-party API
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Remove secrets from shared inputs before transfer
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive runs
Review logs for secret-bearing fields after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write or mutate state through their own runtimes: Kotaemon uses ./ktem_app_data and LightAgent has workflow state, memory, and tool-call surfaces. The profiles do not prove a shared writable directory, but overlapping mutable state makes conflicts plausible if orchestrated together. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or database
IF either agent mutates shared workflow state without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct storage roots
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs during stateful operations
Snapshot state before cross-agent handoff
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent exposes tool calls, tool results, and workflow state, so it can treat upstream outputs as actionable context. Kotaemon produces document-centric answers and citations, which LightAgent could relay or act on without verification. That creates a default cascade path from generated content to downstream actions; the lack of explicit verification makes high appropriate.
conditions: IF LightAgent consumes Kotaemon outputs as authoritative context
IF LightAgent triggers tools or subprocesses based on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action
Require citations or source links for every factual claim
Restrict LightAgent to read-only mode for handoffs
Review high-impact tool calls manually
requires-engineering: add claim-checking against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon touches API keys, chat transcripts, and documents, while LightAgent touches long-term memory, trace data, and workflow state. Those data classes often carry retention and residency obligations, but the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch. The compliance risk is therefore a policy mismatch on shared sensitive data rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF the deployment stores regulated documents or transcripts in LightAgent memory
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two agents
mitigations: Document a shared retention policy
Exclude secrets from long-term memory
Set short log retention for both agents
Confirm deletion/export procedures before production use
requires-engineering: align residency and DPA terms
